Date: 2026-08-28
Tail-Risk Brief v2.0 — Morning Desk Section (pre-market America/Chicago)

# Section 0: Current Positions & Hypotheses

As of August 28, 2026 (pre-market, ~8:20 AM CT). Research framework, not trade recommendations.

**Book snapshot:** Gross delta leverage 4.0x · net delta ≈ -330.1% · premium at risk 40.1% · theta ≈ -0.31%/day · cash liquidity 167.0% of account.
**Model risk appetite:** News collection is intentionally disabled by the cron self-heal rule; this morning brief uses live desk exposures, scenario levels, and updated technicals only.
**Book change vs last published brief:** unchanged symbol roster. Gross delta leverage 4.0x, net delta -330.1%, premium at risk 40.1%, theta -0.31%, cash liquidity 167.0%.

## 1. RTX — aerospace and defense (long)

**Price:** $209.91 close / $212.08 pre-market (+1.0%) | RSI(14): 46.0 | MACD histogram: -2.36
**Fundamentals:** Q2 sales: $24.7B | Q2 backlog: $289B | Q2 free cash flow: $2.9B
**DCF / scenario levels:** Bear $149.53 | Base $210.28 | Bull $225.49
**Thesis:** RTX is a commercial-aerospace and defense backlog-conversion position. Collins, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon must turn a $289 billion backlog into durable organic growth and free cash flow while supply-chain disruption, fixed-price execution, and the GTF powder-metal fleet plan stay controlled.
**Holdings:** Equity · Jan 2027 $230 call | capital 3.0% | exposure +27.2% | premium risk 2.8% | theta -0.02%/day | IV 26.1% | delta +0.37 | 142 DTE
**Catalyst:** Est. Q3 earnings — 2026-10-20 | Trigger: Q3 must keep organic growth, backlog conversion, and free cash flow aligned while supply-chain and GTF fleet-plan costs remain controlled.
**Kill watch:** The thesis breaks if backlog growth stops converting into organic sales and free cash flow, full-year guidance is cut for operational reasons, segment margins deteriorate across more than one business, or GTF and supply-chain costs overwhelm commercial and defense demand.
**Action:** Hold. The thesis is live and the existing size already captures the upside case.

![RTX RSI](charts/2026-08-28/rtx-rsi.png)

![RTX MACD](charts/2026-08-28/rtx-macd.png)

## 2. FRMI — development-stage AI infrastructure (long)

**Price:** $5.92 close / $5.45 pre-market (-7.9%) | RSI(14): 46.5 | MACD histogram: -0.02
**Fundamentals:** Market cap: $5.6B | P/B: 3.5× | Revenue: Pre-commercial
**DCF / scenario levels:** Bear $4.47 | Base $7.26 | Bull $15.00
**Thesis:** A development-stage bet on Project Matador becoming a scarce, gigawatt-scale powered AI campus. Commercial agreements and funded delivery—not headline capacity—must validate it.
**Holdings:** Equity · Dec 2028 $10 call | capital 6.7% | exposure +8.0% | premium risk 3.4% | theta -0.00%/day | IV 118.5% | delta +0.74 | 842 DTE
**Catalyst:** Est. Q3 earnings — 2026-11-10 | Trigger: Q3 must turn the 222 MW anchor contract into funded construction and a credible first-power timetable without another financing shock.
**Kill watch:** No explicit invalidation written.
**Action:** Hold. Momentum is soft, but the thesis still has room if the catalyst path stays intact.

![FRMI RSI](charts/2026-08-28/frmi-rsi.png)

![FRMI MACD](charts/2026-08-28/frmi-macd.png)

## 3. SBUX — turnaround expectations (short)

**Price:** $107.08 close / $107.26 pre-market (+0.2%) | RSI(14): 54.3 | MACD histogram: +0.03
**Fundamentals:** Fiscal Q3 revenue: $9.3B | Global comparable sales: +7.9% | GAAP operating margin: 10.5%
**DCF / scenario levels:** Bear $76.51 | Base $103.99 | Bull $107.93
**Thesis:** Starbucks is a turnaround-expectations short. Better transactions and margins are real, but the short requires Back to Starbucks labor and restructuring spend, China economics, and one-off benefits to keep durable earnings below what the near-high valuation implies.
**Holdings:** Short equity · Sep 2026 $100 put | capital 1.9% | exposure -38.0% | premium risk 1.8% | theta -0.08%/day | IV 30.2% | delta -0.15 | 30 DTE
**Catalyst:** Est. fiscal Q4 earnings — 2026-10-28 | Trigger: Fiscal Q4 must prove transaction growth and margin expansion persist without tariff refunds, restructuring optics, or China-sale comparisons overstating durable earnings.
**Kill watch:** Cover the thesis if Q4 confirms durable positive transactions, clean margin expansion, and stronger cash conversion without material one-off support; invalidate immediately if management raises a credible multi-year earnings path above the short's assumptions.
**Action:** Hold short. Squeeze risk is live, so position size matters more than fresh aggression.

![SBUX RSI](charts/2026-08-28/sbux-rsi.png)

![SBUX MACD](charts/2026-08-28/sbux-macd.png)

## 4. PAYX — payroll and HCM (short)

**Price:** $124.48 close / $126.48 pre-market (+1.6%) | RSI(14): 62.3 | MACD histogram: -0.21
**Fundamentals:** FY26 revenue: $6.51B | FY26 operating income: $2.51B | FY27 adj. EPS guide: +7%–9%
**DCF / scenario levels:** Bear $83.61 | Base $119.93 | Bull $134.87
**Thesis:** Paychex is a payroll and human-capital-management compounder with Paycor integration upside. Fiscal 2027 organic growth, cross-selling, and margin expansion must outrun acquisition amortization, debt costs, labor-market softness, and an expensive recurring-revenue multiple.
**Holdings:** Short equity · Jan 2027 $105 put | capital 31.8% | exposure -53.1% | premium risk 3.3% | theta -0.03%/day | IV 36.3% | delta -0.17 | 142 DTE
**Catalyst:** Est. fiscal Q1 earnings — 2026-09-30 | Trigger: Fiscal Q1 must show organic Management Solutions growth, Paycor cross-selling, and margin progress consistent with fiscal 2027 guidance.
**Kill watch:** Invalidate if organic Management Solutions growth stalls, retention deteriorates, Paycor synergies fail to appear, or fiscal 2027 revenue, margin, and adjusted-EPS guidance is cut without a clearly temporary cause.
**Action:** Hold short. The short is still above the base rail, but the existing book already carries enough exposure.

![PAYX RSI](charts/2026-08-28/payx-rsi.png)

![PAYX MACD](charts/2026-08-28/payx-macd.png)

## 5. DASH — local commerce (short)

**Price:** $223.49 close / $231.89 pre-market (+3.8%) | RSI(14): 60.3 | MACD histogram: +0.59
**Fundamentals:** Q2 Marketplace GOV: $33.1B | Q2 revenue: $4.5B | Q2 adjusted EBITDA: $914M
**DCF / scenario levels:** Bear $146.60 | Base $215.79 | Bull $281.74
**Thesis:** DoorDash is a local-commerce network position. Order and GOV growth, DashPass engagement, Deliveroo integration, and grocery/retail unit economics must compound faster than insurance, regulation, autonomy investment, and international complexity consume the margin upside.
**Holdings:** Short equity · Jan 2027 $200 put | capital 55.3% | exposure -121.4% | premium risk 14.9% | theta -0.10%/day | IV 45.1% | delta -0.21 | 142 DTE
**Catalyst:** Est. Q3 earnings — 2026-11-04 | Trigger: Q3 must preserve organic GOV growth and margin progress while Deliveroo integration and new-category investment remain disciplined.
**Kill watch:** Invalidate if ex-Deliveroo GOV growth decelerates sharply, contribution economics reverse, or integration and regulatory costs overwhelm incremental EBITDA.
**Action:** Hold short. Squeeze risk is live, so position size matters more than fresh aggression.

![DASH RSI](charts/2026-08-28/dash-rsi.png)

![DASH MACD](charts/2026-08-28/dash-macd.png)

## 6. LYV — live events (short)

**Price:** $181.82 close / $180.64 pre-market (-0.6%) | RSI(14): 49.3 | MACD histogram: -0.36
**Fundamentals:** Q2 revenue: $7.7B | Q2 adjusted OI: $817M | Event deferred revenue: $6.4B
**DCF / scenario levels:** Bear $125.61 | Base $180.74 | Bull $188.46
**Thesis:** Live Nation is a live-events demand and venue-capacity position. Record ticket sales and deferred revenue must convert into double-digit adjusted operating income and cash flow while legal remedies, capital intensity, weather, and artist or fan affordability do not impair the flywheel.
**Holdings:** Short equity · Jan 2027 $165 put | capital 55.5% | exposure -152.9% | premium risk 13.9% | theta -0.08%/day | IV 30.9% | delta -0.24 | 142 DTE
**Catalyst:** Est. Q3 earnings — 2026-10-29 | Trigger: Q3 must convert record deferred revenue and ticket demand into the promised second-half and Q4 operating-income acceleration.
**Kill watch:** Invalidate if deferred revenue fails to convert, full-year double-digit adjusted operating income growth is withdrawn, or legal remedies structurally impair ticketing economics.
**Action:** Hold short. The short is still above the base rail, but the existing book already carries enough exposure.

![LYV RSI](charts/2026-08-28/lyv-rsi.png)

![LYV MACD](charts/2026-08-28/lyv-macd.png)

## Risk/Reward ranking (scenario levels; longs ranked upside-to-bull ÷ downside-to-bear)

| Rank | Ticker | Side | Price | Bear | Base | Bull | Ref R/R | Note |
|------|--------|------|-------|------|------|------|---------|------|
| 1 | FRMI | long | $5.45 | $4.47 | $7.26 | $15.00 | ~9.7x | Below base rail |
| 2 | RTX | long | $212.08 | $149.53 | $210.28 | $225.49 | ~0.2x | Weak tape |
| S1 | SBUX | short | $107.26 | $76.51 | $103.99 | $107.93 | squeeze risk | Base-band room |
| S2 | LYV | short | $180.64 | $125.61 | $180.74 | $188.46 | squeeze risk | Base-band room |
| S3 | PAYX | short | $126.48 | $83.61 | $119.93 | $134.87 | squeeze risk | Base-band room |
| S4 | DASH | short | $231.89 | $146.60 | $215.79 | $281.74 | squeeze risk | Base-band room |

**Gemini risk notes:**
- Net short exposure is still extreme at roughly 330%, concentrated mostly in LYV and DASH.
- The highest squeeze-risk shorts this morning are SBUX (RSI 54.3), LYV (RSI 49.3), both still closest to their bull rails.
- Premium at risk remains 40.1% of the account and theta drag is -0.31% per day.
- RTX is the weaker long on momentum, while FRMI still offers the best convex upside versus its bear rail.

*Scenario levels come from the desk hypothesis table. Most names still use market-reference bear/base/bull bands rather than intrinsic-value DCFs, so treat them as scenario rails, not price targets.*
